title.narrative: Developing a business case for plant based raw materials in Durban, South Africa

description.narrative: Developing a business case for plant based raw materials in Durban, South Africa, as many other African countries, is being taunted by the plague of the invasive water hyacinths that are taking over lakes, damaging entire eco-systems and threatening the livelihoods of water communities. In addition, organic waste from important local produce like sugar cane negatively impacts the environment, is often burned or used for unsustainable energy production and adds no value to approximately 300,000 sugar cane farmers. Removing and processing these plants and their bio waste, is very costly and a circular and commercially viable solution is therefore needed. The Dutch consortium of PRM International has developed a technology in which biomass can be transformed into, for example high quality bio composites, feed-stock and bio-concrete, that can be used as a raw material of fibres and proteins for a variety of industries that allows circular production and creates a sustainable income from organic waste and invasive plants. Together with the Durban Green Corridor, the consortium is preparing for future investments in the development of circular and sustainable small scale production plants in South Africa for which Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provides support. The project includes an assessment of a few value chains, including harvesting and supplying of plant and waste streams, the set-up of a pilot plant in Durban and of a joint venture with the Durban Green Corridor, under the name Bridging Worlds, which will directly support 20 jobs during the project. Upon successful completion, the model will be replicated across the country through further investments in 10 to 100 small-scale production plants which will have a positive impact on the environment, create a new income model for local farmers and may result in 1,000 new jobs. Furthermore, a biomass application centre will be opened in February 2020 to research and develop sustainable applications of the raw material for a variety of industries based in South Africa, such as manufacturing, infrastructure, agriculture and fashion.
